name: Tiles, marble and bathroom/kitchen showrooms

problems.words: Customer bought tiles in two lots and the shades don't match on the wall
quick_ideas: Record batch and shade for every design currently in stock, because your records only know the design code
Agree a rule that one order comes from one batch, because "closest to the door" mixes lots.

workzap_build.text: stock by design, size, batch, shade and caliber with location, so every order is allocated from one batch and repeat orders know which batch the client had.

problems.ask_first: Does your system record batch today, or only the design?
problems.free_stops: the batch allocation rules and warehouse flow are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many open orders include tiles from more than one incoming lot, so shade mismatch risk is clear before dispatch.
Keep one reserved area for each open tile order in the warehouse, so staff stop mixing lots during picking.

problems.words: Slabs in the yard, we don't know which are reserved or sold
quick_ideas: Walk the yard once and mark each slab as free, reserved or sold, because it shows what's really available
Photograph every slab with its dimensions, because it ends "which one was it" arguments.

workzap_build.text: a slab register with photos, dimensions, rack location, reserved or sold status and an offcut log.

problems.free_stops: the slab register structure is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the slabs marked reserved in the yard with the sales notes, so you spot what is blocked or still free.
Give one staff member the daily job of updating one yard list of free, reserved and sold slabs, so promises match reality.

problems.words: Breakage in the warehouse and in delivery, no record of who broke what
quick_ideas: Record every breakage for a month by stage (receiving, warehouse, loading, site), because it shows where it really happens
Photograph loads before they leave, because it settles site disputes.

workzap_build.text: a breakage log by stage with photos and monthly cost.

problems.ask_first: Where do you think most breakage happens?
problems.free_stops: the logging process and reporting go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count recent breakages by receiving, warehouse, loading and delivery, so you see where losses are actually starting.
Give one person one breakage notebook kept by the loading area, so every damaged piece is logged the same day.

problems.words: Quotes for a full villa take days and have quantity mistakes
quick_ideas: Keep your last few big quotes as starting points, because rooms repeat
Have a second person check quantities, because errors are costly after cutting.

workzap_build.text: a room-by-room quotation builder with area plus wastage allowance, linked to live stock and prices, as a PDF.

problems.ask_first: How long does a full project quote take today?
problems.free_stops: the quote builder design is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the quantities on recent villa quotes with what was finally supplied, so the rooms causing mistakes stand out.
Give one estimator one notebook for repeated room quantities from finished villas, so future full villa quotes start from real figures.

problems.words: Quote follow-ups get forgotten and the client goes elsewhere
quick_ideas: List every open quote with the date sent, because it shows which have gone cold
Note why lost quotes were lost, because reasons repeat.

workzap_build.text: a quote pipeline with follow-up reminders and won or lost reasons.

problems.ask_first: Who follows up on quotes now?
problems.free_stops: follow-up timings and stages go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many sent quotes have had no follow up since they went out, so missed sales work stops hiding.
Give one person a fixed daily time to review one open quote list, so follow ups happen before clients move on.

problems.words: Countertop measurements are wrong and the slab is cut wrong
quick_ideas: Record the cause of every recent re-cut, because it shows whether it starts at site or in the workshop
Get measurements checked before cutting, because a slab can't be uncut.

workzap_build.text: site measurement capture on tablet linked to the fabrication job, with re-cuts logged by cause.

problems.free_stops: the measurement-to-workshop process is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count recent re cuts by wrong site measurement or wrong workshop cut, so you see where the costly errors begin.
Give one person the handover job between measuring and cutting using one written slab note, so the workshop cuts the intended piece.

problems.words: Installer teams don't show up on the agreed day
quick_ideas: Put every booked installation on one list, because clashes become visible
Confirm with the installer the day before, because surprises drop.

workzap_build.text: an installer schedule with job cards, photos and client sign-off.

problems.ask_first: Do you install yourselves or through partners?
problems.free_stops: scheduling rules and the sign-off flow go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the agreed installation days with the days teams actually arrived, so you see which delays are repeating most.
Keep all booked installation dates in one notebook with one coordinator, so team clashes stop causing missed arrival days.

problems.words: Container delayed and the project waits
quick_ideas: List every container on order with expected dates and the projects waiting on it, because it shows which clients to warn
Check freight and clearance costs on the last container, because they're often missing from prices.

workzap_build.text: a container tracker from order to warehouse, with costs landed into item cost.

problems.free_stops: the tracker and landed-cost method are kept for the solution document; duty questions go to your clearing agent.

extra_ideas.text: Count which open projects are waiting on each delayed container, so you know where the hold up hurts most.
Give one person one list of incoming containers and waiting projects, so updates to sales and site teams stay aligned.

problems.words: Developers pay on long credit and retentions are held
quick_ideas: List every project's balance and retention with its age, because it shows what's really owed
Match invoices to delivery notes once, because missing papers delay payment.

workzap_build.text: a project receivables and retention tracker with ageing and reminders.

problems.ask_first: How do project clients usually pay?
problems.free_stops: the tracking setup goes in the solution document; disputes go to your lawyer.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each project's delivered value with what has been invoiced and collected, so missing paperwork delaying cash shows up.
Give one person one file for each project's invoices and delivery papers, so payment chasing starts from complete records.

problems.words: Architect commissions are calculated by hand and disputed
quick_ideas: Write down the agreed basis for each trade partner, because disputes start where it's unclear
Tie each referral to its project, because otherwise attribution is guesswork.

workzap_build.text: a trade-partner ledger showing referrals, projects and amounts due.

problems.ask_first: How many architects or designers refer to you?
problems.free_stops: ledger setup is kept for the solution document; tax treatment goes to your accountant.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the hand calculated commission on recent referred projects with the original agreed basis, so dispute patterns stand out early.
Give one person one notebook page for every referred project and its commission basis, so referral calculations stay consistent.

problems.words: We don't know margin per project after cutting, wastage and installation
quick_ideas: Work out the real margin on one finished project, because it shows where money leaks
Record wastage and installation cost on the next one, because they're usually missing.

workzap_build.text: margin per project including freight, wastage, fabrication and installation.

problems.ask_first: Can you see the cost of a finished project today?
problems.free_stops: the margin model goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note one finished project's selling price against cutting, wastage and installation costs, so you see where that job lost money.
Give one person the job of writing project extras in one notebook during the work, so true project margin is not guessed later.

never_say: Advice on structural loading, waterproofing, slip resistance, installation safety or material suitability.
For a site or workshop accident, anything other than "call emergency services".
Help with fake or inflated invoices, hidden kickbacks or misdeclared imports.
Advice on import duty, classification or the tax treatment of referral fees.
Legal advice on contract or retention disputes.

sample_reply.person: Our biggest headache is shade variation. Clients come back for more and the new batch is a different shade. What can we do?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this is very solvable. 1. Record batch and shade for every design in stock, because the system only tracks design codes. 2. Agree a rule that each order comes from a single batch, so boxes aren't picked by whatever is nearest. Workzap can do this automatically for you: stock held by batch and shade, every order allocated from one batch, and repeat orders matched to the batch the client had. Would you like me to arrange a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
